newsitem.title: NORWAY: DnB stock jumps on Oslo Bourse.
newsitem.headline: DnB stock jumps on Oslo Bourse.

text.p: Shares in Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's largest bank, rose on Thursday in what could be a reaction to the Bavarian bank megamerger announced this week, dealers said.
DnB shares were up 2.61 percent at 31.40 crowns, a rise of 0.80 crowns, at 1300 GMT. It was the second most traded share at 79 million crowns.
Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, the country's second largest bank, was up 1.29 percent at 26.90 crowns, a rise of 0.50 crowns, in low turnover.
"It could be that we are seeing a reappraisal of the whole sector in view of the Bavarian merger," one dealer said. "Christiania is pulled up by DnB."
"Norwegian bank shares are still cheap by international comparison," the dealer said.
Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG announced on Monday they will merge to create Germany's second largest bank behind Deutsche Bank AG.
